# Endpoint inputs (GENERATED — do not edit by hand)

Generated by `scripts/refresh_spec.py`.
- Part 1: official spec `https://api2.warera.io/openapi.json` — WarEra API version **0.17.4-beta** (37 procedures).
- Part 2: procedures that appear **only** in the community explorer `https://warera.realmarijn.nl/api-explorer` (not in the official spec).

Every procedure is called as `GET https://api2.warera.io/trpc/<procedure>?input=<url-encoded JSON>`.
Both sources render them as POST with a JSON body; that body is the `input` object below.
Neither source has response schemas — see the domain files for observed shapes.
Unknown input keys are silently ignored by the server, so a documented-but-ignored param fails silently.

## company

### `company.getProductionBonus`
Get company production bonus — Retrieves the production bonus information for a specific company. Re-verified live after the v0.27 update (2026-10-26, companies-get-employees patch): the response shrank a lot — strategicBonus, ethicSpecializationBonus and ethicDepositBonus are gone (party ethics and strategic-resource production bonuses were both removed this patch), leaving only depositBonus and total. depositBonus is now always 0 on every company we checked, since this same patch also turned off deposits entirely (country specialization removed) — the field still exists but there's currently no way for it to be non-zero. There is no separate region-level production-bonus endpoint; a company's own +5% core-region bonus (new in v0.27) is applied server-side and isn't broken out anywhere in this response.

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `companyId` | yes | string |  |  | The unique identifier of the company |

### `company.getRecommendedRegionIdsByItemCode`
Get recommended regions by item code — Retrieves a ranked list of regions with production bonuses for a specific item code. Re-verified live after the v0.27 update (2026-10-26): still responds 200 but now always returns an empty array, since this same patch turned off deposits entirely (country specialization removed) and the frontend no longer calls this procedure at all — it's effectively dead, though still technically reachable.

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `itemCode` | yes | string |  | ammo, boots1, boots2, boots3, boots4, boots5, boots6, bread, case1, case2, chest1, chest2, chest3, chest4, chest5, chest6, coca, cocain, concrete, cookedFish, fish, gloves1, gloves2, gloves3, gloves4, gloves5, gloves6, grain, gun, heavyAmmo, helmet1, helmet2, helmet3, helmet4, helmet5, helmet6, iron, jet, knife, lead, lightAmmo, limestone, livestock, oil, pants1, pants2, pants3, pants4, pants5, pants6, paper, petroleum, rifle, scraps, sniper, steak, steel, tank, wood | The item code to find recommended regions for |
| `count` | no | number (min 1) |  |  | Maximum number of regions to return |

## employee

### `employee.getMyEmployees`
Get all of my employees — Retrieves every employee the calling account owns, across all of its companies (v0.27's new hired-employee system). Confirmed live and reachable with our normal, non-premium keys — scoped to whichever account the API key itself belongs to, no parameters taken. Each employee carries its stats (base/trained/revealed), traits, potential, wage, wageExpectation, training/specialization history, happiness breakdown, production bonus breakdown, and an `estimate` of its own hourly output: `production` is raw production POINTS per hour, not money (multiply by gameStat.getPpMoneyValue to get money), and `wage` is money per hour. These sum exactly to the company-level `hourly` totals from employee.getCompanyRoster.

_No input._ Call without `input`.

### `employee.getMyWorkforceSummary`
Get my workforce summary — Retrieves a one-call summary of the calling account's entire workforce across all companies: headcount, how many are trainable today, how many managers are assigned, toolboxes found so far, and hourly totals: `production` in raw production POINTS (multiply by gameStat.getPpMoneyValue to get money), toolbox find rate, and `wageCost` and `managerCost` in money. Confirmed live and reachable with our normal, non-premium keys; no parameters taken.

_No input._ Call without `input`.

### `employee.getCompanyEmployees`
Get a company's employees — Retrieves one company's employee roster — same per-employee shape as employee.getMyEmployees. Confirmed live, public and reachable with our normal, non-premium keys for ANY companyId, not just ones the calling key's account owns.

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `companyId` | yes | string |  |  | The company's ID |

### `employee.getCompanyRoster`
Get a company's full employee roster + hourly totals — Like employee.getCompanyEmployees, but also includes an `hourly` block with the company-wide totals — confirmed these are the exact sum, across every employee, of each one's own `estimate.production`/`estimate.wage`: `{production, toolboxes, wageCost, managerCost, cap}`. `production` is raw production POINTS per hour, NOT money, while `wageCost` and `managerCost` are money per hour, so production has to be converted before subtracting. This is the single best source for a company's current real employee profit: hourly profit = hourly.production * gameStat.getPpMoneyValue - hourly.wageCost - hourly.managerCost, live right now, no lag. Confirmed live, public, reachable with our normal, non-premium keys for any companyId.

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `companyId` | yes | string |  |  | The company's ID |

### `employee.getCompanyEstimate`
Get a company's hourly employee production/wage estimate — Just the `hourly` block from employee.getCompanyRoster, without the employee list — the cheapest call for a company's current real employee profit: hourly profit = production * gameStat.getPpMoneyValue - wageCost - managerCost, in money, live right now (`production` is raw production POINTS per hour, the two costs are already money; no lag, unlike work.getStatsByCompany's daily-aggregated and currently ~1-day-delayed figures). `cap` is the company's current max employee slots. Confirmed live, public, reachable with our normal, non-premium keys for any companyId.

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `companyId` | yes | string |  |  | The company's ID |

### `employee.getManagerPointValue`
Get a manager's per-point value for a company — Retrieves the hourly production one additional Management skill point from a manager would add to this company. Confirmed live, public, reachable with our normal, non-premium keys for any companyId.

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `companyId` | yes | string |  |  | The company's ID |

### `employee.getById`
Get one employee by ID — Retrieves one employee by ID — same shape as one entry of employee.getCompanyRoster's `employees` list. Confirmed live, public, reachable with our normal, non-premium keys; an unknown employeeId returns `null` rather than erroring.

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `employeeId` | yes | string |  |  | The employee's ID (not a user/citizen ID) |

## itemTrading

### `itemTrading.getItemTrading`
Get an item's trading document — Retrieves one item's trading document. values holds the last 30 days, oldest first, with the last row being the current (in-progress) day — confirmed live: avgValue always equals totalValue / totalQuantity on every row, and currentValue equals the last row's avgValue. sellOrders/buyOrders came back empty on every item checked, so they're typed unknown[] here rather than guessed at. An item with no trading record at all (e.g. a toolbox) answers 404 NOT_FOUND, not an empty document.

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `itemCode` | yes | string |  |  | The item code to get the trading document for — a code with no trading record (e.g. a toolbox) 404s |

## work

### `work.getLastByEmployee`
Get last work entry by employee — Retrieves the most recent work entry/entries for one employee (v0.27's new hired-employee system, added when the job market was removed). Confirmed live and reachable with our normal (non-premium) keys. Real output shape unconfirmed: employee IDs come from employee.getMyEmployees, which requires a logged-in session and isn't reachable with an API key, so this could only be probed with a dummy ID (returns an empty array, no error).

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `employeeId` | yes | string |  |  | The employee's ID (not a user/citizen ID) |

### `work.getStatsByEmployee`
Get work stats by employee — Retrieves one hired employee's daily work stats over a period of days (v0.27's new hired-employee system, added when the job market was removed). Confirmed live and reachable with our normal (non-premium) keys — unlike work.getStatsByCompany/ByUserId this does NOT require WarEra Premium. Real output shape unconfirmed: employee IDs come from employee.getMyEmployees, which requires a logged-in session and isn't reachable with an API key, so this could only be probed with a dummy ID (returns an empty array, no error). Likely mirrors the dailyDate/total-style shape of work.getStatsByCompany.

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `employeeId` | yes | string |  |  | The employee's ID (not a user/citizen ID) |
| `days` | no | integer (min 1, max 60) | 30 |  | Number of days of history to return (max 60) — unconfirmed, by analogy with work.getStatsByCompany/ByUserId |

### `work.getStatsByCompany`
Get work stats by company — Retrieves a company's daily work stats over a period of days. Requires the calling account to have WarEra Premium; undocumented in WarEra's own public API reference. Re-verified live after the v0.27 update (2026-10-26, companies-get-employees patch): fields are a subset of selfWork/wage/employeeProd/automatedEngine depending on what that company actually earned that day (zero-valued fields are sometimes omitted entirely, not just set to 0) — employeeProd is production from hired employees (v0.27+); there is no workerProd here (that legacy job-market field only ever appeared on work.getStatsByUserId, scoped to the worker/user, not the hiring company).

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `companyId` | yes | string |  |  | The company ID |
| `days` | no | integer (min 1, max 60) | 30 |  | Number of days of history to return (max 60) |
| `timezone` | no | string |  |  | IANA timezone used to bucket the daily stats, e.g. Europe/Amsterdam |

### `work.getStatsByUserId`
Get work stats by user ID — Retrieves a user's daily work stats (production, wage, self-work vs. automated engine) over a period of days. Requires the calling account to have WarEra Premium; undocumented in WarEra's own public API reference. Re-verified live after the v0.27 update (2026-10-26, companies-get-employees patch): now carries both workerProd (legacy — production as someone else's hired worker under the old job market, which v0.27 removed; present in history, should trend to 0 going forward) and employeeProd (new — production credited from this user's own hired employees).

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `userId` | yes | string |  |  | The user ID to get work stats for |
| `days` | no | integer (min 1, max 60) | 30 |  | Number of days of history to return (max 60) |
| `timezone` | no | string |  |  | IANA timezone used to bucket the daily stats, e.g. Europe/Amsterdam |

### `work.getStatsByWorker`
Get work stats by worker — Retrieves a worker's daily work stats across all companies (not scoped to one company) over a period of days. Requires the calling account to have WarEra Premium; undocumented in WarEra's own public API reference.

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `workerId` | yes | string |  |  | The worker (user) ID |
| `days` | no | integer (min 1, max 60) | 30 |  | Number of days of history to return (max 60) |
| `timezone` | no | string |  |  | IANA timezone used to bucket the daily stats, e.g. Europe/Amsterdam |

### `work.getStatsByWorkerAndCompany`
Get work stats by worker and company — Retrieves a worker's daily work stats scoped to one specific company over a period of days. Requires the calling account to have WarEra Premium; undocumented in WarEra's own public API reference.

| field | req | type | default | options | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `workerId` | yes | string |  |  | The worker (user) ID |
| `companyId` | yes | string |  |  | The company ID |
| `days` | no | integer (min 1, max 60) | 30 |  | Number of days of history to return (max 60) |
| `timezone` | no | string |  |  | IANA timezone used to bucket the daily stats, e.g. Europe/Amsterdam |
